# Diagnostics reference

Every diagnostic code the Glyim compiler can emit, 12 registered in `crates/glyim-diag/errors/codes.toml`. The compiler driver explains one at the terminal with `glyim --explain <CODE>` (for example `glyim --explain T0060`); a bare `glyim --explain` lists every code.

## Lex (E0000–E9999)

Lexing — the lexer could not tokenize the input.

### E0001 — lex error

The lexer could not produce a token from the input at this span. Check for an unterminated literal, an invalid numeric suffix, or a character the lexer does not recognize; the message names the offending byte range.

## Parse (P0000–P9999)

Parsing — the parser did not expect this token.

### P0001 — parse error

The parser did not expect this token in the current grammar position. A leading '|' on a match arm is one known trigger (GAP-0008): parse_pat does not consume a leading pipe, so the arm is rejected with P0001 until that gap closes.

## Type (T0000–T9999)

Type checking — types disagreed with their use.

### T0000 — type error

A generic type-check failure raised by a late pipeline stage (post-monomorphization checks or module loading) that does not yet have a dedicated code. The message carries the specific reason; file an issue if you hit this in normal code.

### T0001 — type mismatch

An expression's type did not match the type expected in that position. The message shows the expected and found types; adjust the expression or the annotation so they agree.

### T0002 — type error

A type error surfaced by the test harness's diagnostic fixtures. Production code should prefer a more specific code; this exists so harness fixtures can assert a distinct type code without aliasing T0001.

### T0050 — non-exhaustive match

A match over an enum did not cover every variant. Add arms for the listed missing variants; the structured diagnostic data carries each missing variant's name and shape so editors can synthesize the arms.

### T0051 — trait not implemented

A method or operation required a trait the receiver type does not implement. Implement the named trait for the named type, or call the operation on a type that already implements it.

### T0060 — await in a non-range for iterable / destructuring loop pattern

.await inside a non-range for iterable or a destructuring loop pattern is rejected by async lowering (GAP-0006). This is a diagnosed gap: every use site gets T0060, so the program is not silently miscompiled. Restructure the loop to await a range-based iterable.

### T0061 — async lowering error

The async lowering pass could not compile this async construct. The message names the construct; common causes are an unsupported await shape or a closure capture that crosses an async boundary.

## Borrow (B0000–B9999)

Borrow checking — the NLL borrow checker rejected the code.

### B0001 — borrow check error

The borrow checker found a violation of the aliasing rules: a mutable borrow aliasing another borrow, a use after a move, or a reference escaping its lifetime. The message identifies the conflicting borrows.

## Comptime (C0000–C9999)

Compile-time evaluation — a const/compile-time step failed.

### C0001 — comptime / macro error

A macro expansion or compile-time evaluation failed. For macros, check the rule arity and the captured tokens; for const evaluation, check that the evaluated expression is constant and terminates within the step budget.

## Internal (X0000–X9999)

Internal — a compiler-side invariant or setup failure.

### X0000 — internal compiler error / warning

An internal diagnostic: either a compiler ICE surfaced as a user-facing error (severity Error) or an internal warning (severity Warning). If you see this as an Error on valid input, it is a compiler bug — please file an issue with a reproduction.
